solution:
\(\dfrac{\text{circumference}}{\text{area}} = \dfrac{2\pi r}{\pi r^2} = \dfrac{2}{r}\).

Given \(\dfrac{2}{r} = \dfrac{2}{7}\), so \(r = 7\).

\(\therefore\) circumference \(= 2\pi r = 2\pi \times 7 = 14\pi\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the textbook.

\(44 = \dfrac{160}{360} \times C\)

solution:
The perimeter of a sector is the arc plus the two bounding radii.

Arc \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 44 = 11\) cm.

Perimeter \(= 11 + 7 + 7 = 25\) cm.

This agrees with the answer printed in the textbook.

solution:
Curved surface area of a cylinder \(= 2\pi r h\).

\(440 = 2\pi \times 5 \times h = 10\pi h\)

\(\therefore h = \dfrac{440}{10\pi} = \dfrac{44}{\pi}\) cm.

The answer is left in terms of \(\pi\) because the question gives no value for it. This agrees with the answer printed in the textbook.
